forecasts.question: Will Iran take a new concrete action to fully close the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping (confirmed by UKMTO/NAVCENT advisory and two TIER1 sources) before EOD 2026-06-09?
forecasts.delta_reason: Judge cold-start override (cold 0.55 rejected, DA 0.25 partially rejected). June 6 IRGC attacks on four tankers are real escalation but constitute continuation of pre-existing interdiction posture — ambiguity rule continuation-exclusion is operative. Strait has been de facto closed since March 2026 mine-laying; interdicting specific tankers does not constitute a new discrete closure action (new mine-laying with coordinates, formal exclusion order) as resolution criteria require. US strikes on Goruk/Qeshm radar sites June 6 are new US action, not Iranian closure declaration. Dual-source UKMTO/NAVCENT advisory for new discrete closure event not yet issued. p reduced 0.40→0.35: lower than inherited to reflect strict ambiguity-rule application, but above DA's 0.25 because June 6 tanker attacks are genuine escalation and the NAVCENT advisory gap may close before June 9.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if UKMTO NAVAREA IX issues an advisory confirming a NEW discrete Iranian action (mine-laying citing new coordinates post-2026-06-02, formal closure declaration/exclusion order, or IRGC seizure/attack on a commercial vessel) AND two TIER1 sources (Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Bloomberg) independently confirm before EOD 2026-06-09. Continuation of pre-existing mine-laying campaign without new coordinates or declaration does NOT satisfy this criterion.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: UKMTO NAVAREA IX advisory + NAVCENT press statement (both required for mine-laying) OR two independent TIER1 citing a formal Iranian closure declaration. NAVCENT-confirmed new IRGC attack on a commercial vessel counts if corroborated by a second TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Repetition of existing warnings does NOT count. Continuation of pre-existing mine-laying or interdiction posture without new coordinates or declaration = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iranian state-media assertions without UKMTO/NAVCENT confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. IRGC firing on transiting vessels without new formal closure declaration or new mine-laying coordinates = AMBIGUOUS — does not automatically satisfy resolution. If June 6 tanker attacks receive UKMTO/NAVCENT advisory explicitly citing a new discrete closure-enforcement action, human review required.

Ambiguity rule and source rule updated per Judge hygiene review.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading specifying an election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official records (knesset.gov.il) or Knesset Speaker statement reported by Haaretz/Times of Israel/JNS required. Speaker statement alone without official record confirmation = AMBIGUOUS.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition formally lose its Knesset majority (confirmed by a roll-call vote) before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: SUNDAY REVIEW (cold-start audit). Cold-start gap 50pp (inherited 0.35, cold 0.85). Judge ruling: cold-start of 0.85 REJECTED — it conflates UTJ/Shas informal departures reducing operational seat count to ~60 since July 2025 with a formal roll-call majority loss, which resolution criteria require. The 106-0 dissolution bill vote June 2 demonstrates coalition retains functional working majority on chosen votes. Electoral polling showing 49-51 projected seats is NOT the same as formal seat-count defeat. Controlled-dissolution scenario is dominant; Netanyahu engineering managed exit does NOT trigger YES. Inherited 0.35 is stale (19 days) and understates genuine fragility. Judge sets at 0.45: reflects real fragility (60 seats < 61 threshold since July 2025) and risk that Haredi draft exemption revival fails, triggering formal defection and roll-call defeat before Oct 27. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a formal Knesset roll-call vote (confidence vote, budget vote, or substantive non-dissolution plenary vote) confirms that the coalition has fewer than 61 supporting votes, before 2026-10-27. Informal party withdrawals, electoral polling projections, and dissolution bill votes do NOT satisfy this criterion.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official plenary voting records (knesset.gov.il) required. Haaretz/Times of Israel/JNS report of the vote result as secondary confirmation. Roll-call record must be accessible and independently verifiable.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Controlled dissolution process (coalition engineering its own dissolution to call elections) does NOT satisfy YES — this is managed exit, not forced majority loss. If coalition loses a vote because it chose to abstain rather than because it lacked the votes, resolve AMBIGUOUS. Electoral polling showing <61 projected seats does NOT satisfy resolution. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.
